heuristics: Ask "What is the paper's central verb?" Predict, generate, represent, detect, segment, reconstruct, optimize, control, retrieve, reason, adapt, secure, accelerate, evaluate, or compose.
Classify by the central technical contribution, not the headline application. An AI drug-design paper may be generation, optimization, prediction, or a benchmark depending on its actual novelty.
Separate task from technique. "Diffusion" is usually a model family tag; "3D shape generation" is the task. "LoRA" is an adaptation mechanism; the adapted task remains prediction, generation, etc.
Allow multi-label classification. Pick one primary node and up to two secondary nodes; use cross-cutting tags for the rest.
Keep the application domain (healthcare, robotics, biology, climate, …) as a tag rather than duplicating the tree per field.
Add branches only when they improve retrieval. Prefer a stable, understandable top level over a deep tree that is hard to maintain.
Record confidence. If an abstract is vague, mark the label as uncertain and revisit when reading the paper.
